title: US measles cases hit 2,318 in 2026, surpassing last year's total: CDC
snippet:
The majority of measles cases in 2026 have been confirmed among children and teenagers aged 19 and younger, according to the CDC. About one in 10 children under age 5 have been hospitalized.

About 93% of cases are among people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown, CDC data shows. [...] However, CDC data shows vaccination rates have been lagging in recent years. During the 2024 to 2025 school year, 92.5% of kindergartners received the MMR vaccine, according to data. This is lower than the 92.7% seen in the previous school year and the 95.2% seen in the 2019 to 2020 school year, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Some public health specialists previously told ABC News they believe the U.S. is on track to lose the elimination status it earned in 2000. [...] ## Live

# US measles cases hit 2,318 in 2026, surpassing last year's total: CDC

This marks the highest number of cases recorded since 1991.

The number of confirmed measles cases in the U.S. so far this year has hit 2,318, surpassing the total reported for all last year, according to data updated Friday from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

title: U.S. measles cases hit 35-year record with months left in 2026
snippet:
# U.S. measles cases hit 35-year record with months left in 2026

Data from Johns Hopkins University’s U.S. measles tracker shows the nation reported 2,295 cases as of Tuesday. That count surpasses last year’s total of 2,289.

The United States has now reported the most measles cases in any year since 1991, not only surpassing all of last year’s record total, but also reaching the highest level in 35 years, with more than five months still remaining in 2026.

title: Measles
snippet:
WHO continues to strengthen the Global Measles and Rubella Laboratory Network (GMRLN) to ensure timely diagnosis of measles and track the virus’ spread to assist countries in coordinating targeted vaccination activities and reduce deaths from this vaccine-preventable disease.

### The IA2030 Measles & Rubella Partnership [...] Routine measles vaccination, combined with mass immunization campaigns in countries with high case rates are crucial for reducing global measles deaths. The measles vaccine has been in use for about 60 years and costs less than US$ 1 per child. The measles vaccine is also used in emergencies to stop outbreaks from spreading. The risk of measles outbreaks is particularly high amongst refugees, who should be vaccinated as soon as possible. [...] ## WHO response

In 2020, WHO and global stakeholders endorsed the Immunization Agenda 2021–2030. The Agenda aims to achieve the regional targets as a core indicator of impact, positioning measles as a tracer of a health system’s ability to deliver essential childhood vaccines.

WHO published the Measles and rubella strategic frameworkin 2020, establishing seven necessary strategic priorities to achieve and sustain the regional measles and rubella elimination goals.
